decisions.quote:
Title: The Effect Of Thinking About Being Excluded By God On Well-Being: A Replication And Extension
Author: Anna R. George
Abstract: Diverse samples and replication are two important aspects of scientific research. Our research replicates a previous study, which examined how Christians being led to believe God will either include or exclude them influenced well-being scores.

The SMART single-blind trial explicitly interrogates earlier verbal/intellectual gains under strongercontrols, with actualcomparisons to Cassidy2011pilot verbalIQ, Hayes/Stewart2016verbal/blockdesign/activecomputercontrol findings, Amd/Rochedosageeffect inBangladesh andThirus2016controlledRavenintelligence claim. Current IQ/MatrixReasoning and training-level analyses are actualtests, not onlyinterventionreuse. Printed references and documented differing designs/samples distinguishpublishedreports from20Cassidy2016; no assertion of every participant disjoint across uninspected originalbodies. All outcomesremainunknown rather than transferredfromgenerictraininggain. This decision resolves this specific described/named original identity, without promoting the blind coding or transferring an outcome.
